editorial.titleTr: Kim Seung-won Confirmation Report Forced Through... Defiant Challenge to Public Will
summaryTr: Democratic Party pushes through confirmation report on Kim Seung-won despite public opposition
Vote held after just two days, proceeding despite insufficient resolution of suspicions
Concerns of plummeting approval ratings if appointment is forced through, causing public backlash
editorial.bodyTr: The Democratic Party of Korea unilaterally adopted the confirmation hearing report on Kim Seung-won, the nominee for Justice Minister, at the National Assembly's Legislation and Judiciary Committee on September 17, 2026. Despite significant public opposition shown in opinion polls, the party forced a vote just two days after the hearing, and the suspicions raised were not sufficiently addressed. The article argued that if the president pushes ahead with the appointment, it could clash with public sentiment, leading to a decline in approval ratings and a weakening of governmental momentum.

summaryTr: U.S. Federal Reserve Raises Benchmark Rate for First Time in Three Years, Signals Further Increases
Central Banks Shift to Tightening Policy as Energy and AI Investment Fuel Inflation Pressures
South Korea Braces for Price Stability and Fiscal Austerity as Household Debt Burden Grows
editorials.bodyTr: The U.S. Federal Reserve raised its benchmark interest rate by 0.25 percentage points for the first time in more than three years since July 2023, and signaled additional increases ahead. The United States has clearly shifted course toward tightening policy as inflationary pressures intensified due to rising energy prices and expanded artificial intelligence investments. Given South Korea's substantial household debt and lending rate burdens, the country should prioritize price stability in its policy and reduce fiscal expansion to prepare for potential shocks.

summaryTr: Democratic Party in collision over whether to admit video evidence of minor sexual assault victim interviews

Pan-opposition hardliners reject even prosecutor-origin candidates, causing confusion
editorials.bodyTr: Conflict has intensified within the Democratic Party over whether to admit video recordings of interviews with underage sexual abuse victims as evidence. A revised bill led by hardliners stipulates that video recordings of interviews conducted by prosecutors cannot be used as evidence even if recorded. An editorial criticized the ruling coalition hardliners for exacerbating confusion by rejecting even candidates on the grounds that they are former prosecutors.

editorial.titleTr: [Editorial] Prosecutors Question Nominee's Pro-Yoon Ties While Ignoring Investigative Competence
summaryTr: The vetting of the candidate for head of the Serious Crimes Division is degenerating into a controversy over pro-Yoon leanings.
The Ministry of the Interior and Safety is defending based on investigative track record, while the opposition continues demanding resignation amid partisan wrangling.
Verification of investigative competence and neutrality is being undermined by factional conflict.
editorial.bodyTr: The political conflict surrounding the candidate for the head of the Serious Crimes Investigation Office is intensifying. The Ministry of the Interior and Safety is denying the candidate's pro-Yoon inclination and defending based on past investigative records, while the opposition continues the political dispute by demanding resignation. There are concerns that the verification of the SCI director, where investigative capacity and neutrality should be emphasized, has deteriorated into partisan confrontation, resulting in the loss of essential verification functions.

editorial.titleTr: [Editorial] Prosecution Withdrawal and Reelection Debate Must End for Press Conference to Prove Change
summaryTr: President Lee Jae-myung holds a press conference on the 18th, but concrete changes are essential to recover his approval ratings.
He must first end controversies over the dismissal of charges and constitutional revision for consecutive terms, and offer a clear apology for failures in real estate policy.
Without fundamental improvements in inappropriate personnel appointments and the president-centric governing style, the press conference will be meaningless.
editorial.bodyTr:
President Lee Jae-myung has decided to hold a press conference on the 18th amid declining approval ratings for his administration. While he says he will answer questions about pending national issues without restrictions, simply opening a channel for communication will not be enough to win back public trust. An opinion poll released yesterday by the Korean Social Opinion Research Institute showed that negative assessments outweighed positive ones across all age groups, including those in their 40s and 50s who had strongly supported the ruling party. The situation calls for clear reflection on the overall direction of state affairs, which has lost public confidence.

The first matters to address are the withdrawal of prosecution and the proposed constitutional amendment for consecutive reelection, both related to the president's legal risks. The confusion surrounding the withdrawal of prosecution and public skepticism about pursuing a constitutional amendment for reelection have been cited as burdens on state affairs by both the opposition and within the ruling party itself. Since these issues directly concern the president personally, he must end the controversy by explicitly stating that he will abandon efforts to withdraw the prosecution and that under no circumstances will he seek reelection. Abandoning the stubbornness and self-righteousness that shake judicial and constitutional order is the bare minimum starting point for a recovery in approval ratings.

The president must also apologize for the failure of real estate policy that has failed to address citizens' actual living conditions and present supplementary measures. The government has caused market distortions such as soaring jeonse and monthly rental prices through measures like tax pressure on non-resident single-home owners, yet has only cited the justification of eliminating speculation. If the administration fails to demonstrate how it will correct this apparent incompetence and policy misjudgment, it will not be able to suppress the backlash from young people and the middle class that is now emerging.

Decisive action on personnel failures is also necessary. If the government pushes forward with appointments despite putting forward underqualified ministerial candidates and drawing public outrage, the press conference will lose all credibility. In particular, bold measures are needed to make Justice Minister nominee Kim Seung-won, who has caused controversy through inappropriate solicitation, step down voluntarily or withdraw his nomination. Attempting to push through his appointment based on a "toothless confirmation hearing" would only add fuel to public alienation.

President Lee has thus far demonstrated a hands-on governance style in which he directly oversees all matters. As a result, the president's position has become the guideline, rigorous verification has disappeared, and policies disconnected from the people's lives have driven livelihoods into ruin. The public is currently sending a strong signal that it wants sincere apologies about the flawed direction of state affairs and concrete change. If the president says something different, the press conference might as well not happen.

editorial.title: Costly capital
editorial.body: Higher borrowing costs demand reforms that lift productivity, strengthen finances Cheap money has enjoyed a remarkably long run. Its retirement is now harder to deny, forcing South Korea to rethink policies built around the assumption that capital will remain cheap. This week, the 10-year US Treasury yield broke above 5 percent while the Federal Reserve raised its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to 3.75 to 4 percent, its first increase since July 2023. For more than two decades, cheap capital, energy and labor helped economies absorb inefficiencies that otherwise would have been costly. As that cushion shrinks, the nation should stop building policy around the expectation that rates will soon return to their old lows. Long-term yields are being shaped by more than near-term inflation. Oil above $100 a barrel is adding to price pressures as conflict persists in the Middle East. The vast sums being poured into artificial intelligence infrastructure are also competing for global savings. US fiscal policy is another strain. Gross public debt has climbed above 110 percent of gross domestic product, and investors are demanding a larger premium to hold long-dated government bonds. The special advantage once enjoyed by Treasurys as exceptionally liquid and safe assets has also weakened. There is a tempting shortcut. Governments can issue more short-term debt to avoid locking in today's elevated long-term yields. But that merely brings the problem closer. With more debt maturing sooner, refinancing becomes costlier if rates stay high. A changing investor base, with more price-sensitive and leveraged participants in bond markets, can make benchmark yields more volatile. Korea is already feeling the shock. The 10-year Treasury bond yield has risen above 4.6 percent, reaching its highest level since October 2022. Higher government bond yields eventually feed into corporate borrowing costs and bank lending rates, squeezing businesses and households. The Bank of Korea has also tightened, raising its policy rate to 3 percent over two consecutive meetings in July and August. It was the first back-to-back tightening since January 2023, when the BOK completed a rate-hike cycle that began in April 2022. The gap with the Fed has widened to as much as 1 percentage point, with a weaker won and heavy household leverage adding to the strain. Yet simply matching every Fed move would be poor monetary policy. The BOK should set clear conditions for further increases and weigh their timing against domestic inflation, exchange rates and credit conditions. Household credit has already exceeded 2,000 trillion won ($1.45 trillion), and corporate debt is nearing that scale. Higher interest expenses will weigh most heavily on borrowers with little room to absorb them. Financial support should therefore be selective. Extending loans indefinitely can conceal losses rather than resolve them. Fiscal policy faces its own burden. Large-scale government borrowing can put further upward pressure on market rates, and interest payments consume more of the budget. Korea should trim nonessential spending to preserve primary fiscal stability. When capital is expensive, competitiveness depends on the output generated by each unit of investment. 높은 차입 비용은 생산성을 높이고 재정을 강화하는 개혁을 요구한다

저금리의 시대가 놀랍도록 오랫동안 지속되어 왔다. 이제 그 종말을 더 이상 부정할 수 없게 되었으며, 이는 한국이 자본이 계속 저렴할 것이라는 가정 위에 지어진 정책들을 재검토하도록 강요하고 있다. 이번 주 미국 10년물 국채 수익률이 5퍼센트를 넘어섰고, 연방준비제도는 기준금리를 25베이시스포인트 인상하여 3.75에서 4퍼센트로 올렸는데, 이는 2023년 7월 이후 처음이다. 20년 이상 저렴한 자본, 에너지, 노동력은 경제가 그렇지 않으면 비용이 많이 들었을 비효율성을 흡수하도록 도와왔다. 이러한 쿠션이 줄어들면서 한국은 금리가 곧 과거의 낮은 수준으로 돌아올 것이라는 기대를 바탕으로 정책을 수립하기를 멈춰야 한다.

장기 수익률은 단기 인플레이션보다 더 많은 요인에 의해 결정되고 있다. 배럴당 100달러를 넘는 석유는 중동 분쟁이 지속되면서 물가 상승압을 가중하고 있다. 인공지능 기반시설에 쏟아지는 막대한 자금도 세계 저축에 경쟁하고 있다. 미국의 재정정책도 또 다른 부담이다. 국내총생산 대비 정부 총채무가 110퍼센트를 넘어섰으며, 투자자들은 장기 정부채를 보유하기 위해 더 큰 프리미엄을 요구하고 있다. 과거 국채가 누렸던 예외적으로 유동성이 높고 안전한 자산이라는 특별한 이점도 약해졌다.

유혹적인 지름길이 있다. 정부가 더 많은 단기채를 발행해 오늘의 높아진 장기 수익률을 고정하는 것을 피할 수 있다. 하지만 이는 문제를 더 가까워지게 할 뿐이다. 더 많은 채무가 더 빨리 만기되면서 금리가 높은 상태로 유지될 경우 차환 비용이 높아진다. 채권시장에 더 민감하고 레버리지를 활용하는 참여자들이 증가하는 투자자 기반의 변화는 기준 수익률을 더 변동성 있게 만들 수 있다.

한국은 이미 충격을 받고 있다. 미국 10년물 국채 수익률이 4.6퍼센트 이상으로 올라 2022년 10월 이후 최고 수준에 도달했다. 높아진 정부채 수익률은 결국 기업의 차입 비용과 은행의 대출금리로 이어져 기업과 가계를 옭아맨다. 한국은행도 긴축했으며, 지난 7월과 8월 두 달에 연속으로 정책금리를 3퍼센트로 인상했다. 이는 2023년 1월 이후 처음의 연속 인상으로, 당시 한은은 2022년 4월부터 시작된 금리 인상 사이클을 완료했다. 연방준비제도와의 격차가 최대 1퍼센트 포인트까지 벌어졌으며, 약세 원화와 높은 가계 레버리지가 부담을 더하고 있다.

하지만 단순히 연준의 모든 움직임을 따라가는 것은 좋지 못한 통화정책이 될 것이다. 한국은행은 추가 인상에 대한 명확한 조건을 설정하고 그 시기를 국내 인플레이션, 환율, 신용 상황에 비춰 판단해야 한다. 가계신용이 이미 2,000조 원을 초과했고, 기업 채무도 이에 가까워지고 있다. 높아진 이자 비용은 이를 감당할 여지가 적은 차입자들에게 가장 무거운 부담이 될 것이다. 따라서 금융 지원은 선별적이어야 한다. 대출을 무한정 연장하는 것은 손실을 해결하기보다 감추는 것일 뿐이다.

재정정책도 자체의 부담을 안고 있다. 대규모 정부 차입은 시장 금리에 추가적인 상승 압력을 가할 수 있으며, 이자 지불이 예산의 더 많은 부분을 차지한다. 한국은 기초 재정 안정성을 유지하기 위해 필수불급한 지출을 줄여야 한다. 자본이 비쌀 때 경쟁력은 각 단위의 투자에서 나오는 산출량에 달려 있다. 이는 시장 진입 장벽을 낮추고, 노동시장에 더 큰 유연성을 주며, 생산성에 대한 인센티브를 강화하는 규제 개혁을 요구한다. 금리는 결국 떨어질 수 있지만, 언제일지는 아무도 모른다. 국가는 자본이 재정 과다 도입과 비생산적 투자를 드러낼 만큼 오랫동안 비싼 상태로 유지될 준비를 해야 한다. 저금리는 한때 정책결정자들이 어려운 결정을 미룰 수 있게 해주었다. 그 시대는 가고 있다. 한국은 더 이상 낮은 생산성, 무분별한 레버리지, 방향 잘못된 자본을 용인할 여유가 없다. 이제의 과제는 높아진 차입 비용이 성장의 항구적인 장애물이 되기 전에 자본의 각 단위가 측정 가능한 수익을 내도록 하는 것이다.

editorials.title: Costly capital
editorials.body: Higher borrowing costs demand reforms that lift productivity, strengthen finances Cheap money has enjoyed a remarkably long run. Its retirement is now harder to deny, forcing South Korea to rethink policies built around the assumption that capital will remain cheap. This week, the 10-year US Treasury yield broke above 5 percent while the Federal Reserve raised its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to 3.75 to 4 percent, its first increase since July 2023. For more than two decades, cheap capital, energy and labor helped economies absorb inefficiencies that otherwise would have been costly. As that cushion shrinks, the nation should stop building policy around the expectation that rates will soon return to their old lows. Long-term yields are being shaped by more than near-term inflation. Oil above $100 a barrel is adding to price pressures as conflict persists in the Middle East. The vast sums being poured into artificial intelligence infrastructure are also competing for global savings. US fiscal policy is another strain. Gross public debt has climbed above 110 percent of gross domestic product, and investors are demanding a larger premium to hold long-dated government bonds. The special advantage once enjoyed by Treasurys as exceptionally liquid and safe assets has also weakened. There is a tempting shortcut. Governments can issue more short-term debt to avoid locking in today's elevated long-term yields. But that merely brings the problem closer. With more debt maturing sooner, refinancing becomes costlier if rates stay high. A changing investor base, with more price-sensitive and leveraged participants in bond markets, can make benchmark yields more volatile. Korea is already feeling the shock. The 10-year Treasury bond yield has risen above 4.6 percent, reaching its highest level since October 2022. Higher government bond yields eventually feed into corporate borrowing costs and bank lending rates, squeezing businesses and households. The Bank of Korea has also tightened, raising its policy rate to 3 percent over two consecutive meetings in July and August. It was the first back-to-back tightening since January 2023, when the BOK completed a rate-hike cycle that began in April 2022. The gap with the Fed has widened to as much as 1 percentage point, with a weaker won and heavy household leverage adding to the strain. Yet simply matching every Fed move would be poor monetary policy. The BOK should set clear conditions for further increases and weigh their timing against domestic inflation, exchange rates and credit conditions. Household credit has already exceeded 2,000 trillion won ($1.45 trillion), and corporate debt is nearing that scale. Higher interest expenses will weigh most heavily on borrowers with little room to absorb them. Financial support should therefore be selective. Extending loans indefinitely can conceal losses rather than resolve them. Fiscal policy faces its own burden. Large-scale government borrowing can put further upward pressure on market rates, and interest payments consume more of the budget. Korea should trim nonessential spending to preserve primary fiscal stability. When capital is expensive, competitiveness depends on the output generated by each unit of investment. That calls for regulatory reform to lower barriers to market entry, give labor markets greater flexibility and strengthen incentives for productivity. Rates may eventually fall, but nobody knows when. The country should prepare for capital to remain expensive long enough to expose overextended finances and unproductive investment. Cheap money once allowed policymakers to postpone hard decisions. That era is receding. Korea no longer has the luxury of tolerating low productivity, reckless leverage or misdirected capital. The task now is to make every unit of capital yield measurable return before higher borrowing costs turn into a permanent drag on growth. 재정정책도 자체의 부담을 안고 있다. 대규모 정부 차입은 시장 금리에 추가적인 상승 압력을 가할 수 있으며, 이자 지불이 예산의 더 많은 부분을 차지한다. 한국은 기초 재정 안정성을 유지하기 위해 필수불급한 지출을 줄여야 한다. 자본이 비쌀 때 경쟁력은 각 단위의 투자에서 나오는 산출량에 달려 있다. 이는 시장 진입 장벽을 낮추고, 노동시장에 더 큰 유연성을 주며, 생산성에 대한 인센티브를 강화하는 규제 개혁을 요구한다. 금리는 결국 떨어질 수 있지만, 언제일지는 아무도 모른다. 국가는 자본이 재정 과다 도입과 비생산적 투자를 드러낼 만큼 오랫동안 비싼 상태로 유지될 준비를 해야 한다. 저금리는 한때 정책결정자들이 어려운 결정을 미룰 수 있게 해주었다. 그 시대는 가고 있다. 한국은 더 이상 낮은 생산성, 무분별한 레버리지, 방향 잘못된 자본을 용인할 여유가 없다. 이제의 과제는 높아진 차입 비용이 성장의 항구적인 장애물이 되기 전에 자본의 각 단위가 측정 가능한 수익을 내도록 하는 것이다.

summaryTr: Government extends moratorium on mandatory occupancy requirement in land transaction permit zones for one more year through end of next year.
Eases housing instability by including tenant lease renewal contracts within the grace period.
Complementary policy that simultaneously opens exit routes for multi-property owners while strengthening tenant protections.
editorial.bodyTr: The government has decided to extend by one year until the end of next year the application deadline for exemptions from mandatory occupancy requirements in land transaction permit zones, originally set to expire at the end of this year. editorials.titleTr: Revised Farmland Law' Backlash Over Neglect of Rural Realities
summaryTr: The revised Agricultural Land Act, implemented on the 28th of last month, is facing growing backlash in rural areas.
The measure mandates penalties for owners who do not farm the land, aiming to establish the principle of owner-cultivators.
Concerns have been raised about infringement on property rights of elderly farmers and the creation of innocent victims.
editorials.bodyTr: Backlash is spreading in rural communities over the revised Agricultural Land Act that went into effect on the 28th of last month. The core of this law is to mandate disposal orders for agricultural land owners who are not actively farming. While the intention is to prevent agricultural land speculation and establish the principle of owner-cultivator farming, critics point out that it infringes on the property rights of elderly farmers and could create numerous victims among well-intentioned landholders. The revised Agricultural Land Act changed agricultural land disposal provisions from discretionary regulations to mandatory regulations.
